assembly.name: Suspension — front (MacPherson) & steering
assembly.description: MacPherson strut front axle (dossier §5): struts with coil springs and PASSIVE sport dampers (this car has no DCC), the newly-developed 'low wishbone' lower control arms with track-stabilising scrub radius, steering knuckles, anti-roll bar with drop links, and the electromechanical progressive-ratio steering rack. Ride height 20 mm below a base Golf.

parts.name: Front subframe
parts.description: Front subframe carrying the control arms, rack, and ARB; aluminium content on the MQB front axle (dossier §5). The engine's dogbone mount also lands here (mount modelled with engine ancillaries in Phase 7). R7: the subframe must be located on its alignment pins when refitted or the steering sits off-centre.

torqueSpec.note: Subframe-to-body and console-to-body — TTY, ALWAYS replace (R7)

parts.name: MacPherson struts (spring + passive damper) ×2
parts.description: Passive sport front struts, 5Q0413031EC — the dealer catalogue's 'Golf R without DCC' family, correct for this car (confirm via the absent J250 module) (R7). ~20 mm lower than GTI. Strut piston-rod nut 60 Nm (M14×1.5); the strut-to-knuckle clamp bolt takes a 14 mm triple-square (R12) but its torque was NOT found verbatim — per erWin.

torqueSpec.note: Strut piston-rod nut M14×1.5 (R7); strut-to-knuckle clamp torque NONE FOUND — per erWin

knownIssues: Top-mount bearings creak/knock on full lock — a known Mk7 wear item (R7).

parts.name: Lower control arms ('low wishbone') ×2
parts.description: The Mk7's newly-developed low wishbone with track-stabilising scrub radius (dossier §5): two inboard bushes on the subframe, ball joint outboard under the knuckle. R7: left arm 5Q0407151J (also 151R, superseded 5WA407151); the right side 5Q0407152J is an inferred mirror — verify. Console/rear bush bolts 70 Nm + 180° TTY, renew.

torqueSpec.note: LCA console-to-body — TTY, renew (R7); front pivot bolt N10640501 M12×1.5×80

knownIssues: Rear (console) bush wear — the classic Mk7 MOT advisory: knock + vague steering (R7).

parts.name: Steering knuckles / bearing housings ×2
parts.description: Uprights tying strut, ball joint, tie rod and hub together; the driveshaft's outer CV splines into the hub here. Torque shown is the main hub/axle bolt (dossier §2 table). Hub-unit-to-knuckle bolts 70 Nm + 90° (R7).

torqueSpec.note: Hub/axle bolt WHT005437 (smooth-face 8.8, 12-pt M16×1.5×70), single-use (R6/R12). ElsaWin shows a +90° variant, and a RIBBED ~10.9 bolt exists taking only 70 Nm + 90° — physically identify the bolt before torquing

parts.name: Anti-roll bar, front
parts.description: Front ARB on the subframe, coupled to the struts through drop links (dossier §5). R7: family 5Q0411303, Ø ~23.2 mm on the 4WD car — vendor-sized (Powerflex), not VW-published; verify.

parts.name: ARB drop links, front ×2
parts.description: Short ball-jointed links from the ARB ends up to the strut bodies.
knownIssues: Knock over small bumps when worn — cheap fix, common at UK mileages (R7).

parts.name: Steering rack (electromechanical, progressive ratio)
parts.description: Rack-mounted parallel-axis (APA) electromechanical steering with the R's PROGRESSIVE variable-pitch rack as standard — 2.1 turns / 380° lock-to-lock, ratio quickening off-centre (R7). Family 5Q1423051/053 with control unit J500 integrated on the rack; any rack replacement or alignment needs coding + the G85 steering-angle basic setting.

torqueSpec.note: Rack-to-subframe, renew (R7). R12's chart carries 70 Nm + 90° — CONFLICT, verify

knownIssues: MQB EPS rack knock over rough surfaces — subject of a VW TSB (R7).

parts.name: Tie rods + ends ×2
parts.description: Tie rods from the rack ends to the knuckles' steering arms; the outer ends are the toe-adjustment point.

torqueSpec.note: Track-rod end to knuckle (R7). Inner tie-rod and locknut torques NONE FOUND — per erWin; steering-UJ pinch bolt 30 Nm (M8×35, renew)
